history.period: Ancient; referenced in the Gurucharitra (~700 years ago); Haripur founded 1768
history.summary: The Sangameshwar Temple is an old Shiva temple in Haripur village, Sangli district, at the sangam (confluence) of the Krishna and Warna (Varna) rivers - hence the name Sangameshwar. The Gurucharitra (written ~700 years ago) mentions this temple, and Shiva is worshipped here under the name Markandeya. In 1768 Govind Hari Patwardhan settled Brahmins here, giving the town the name Haripur after Hari Patwardhan. The temple complex holds a Shivalinga in the main sanctum with a pradakshina path lined with small shrines (Narasimha, Dattatreya, Kalbhairav, Sant Dnyaneshwar, Vitthal-Rukmini, Hanuman, Shani) and a Vishnu temple near the entrance. Shravan month is its peak season, with a big fair and thousands of devotees on Mondays.

name: Sangameshwar Temple
town: Haripur (Miraj taluka; CSV town 'Sangli' is the district HQ, ~4 km away)
town_description: Haripur is a village on the banks of the Krishna river about 4 km from Sangli city, at the confluence of the Krishna and Warna (Varna) rivers. It was developed by the Patwardhans (Govind Hari Patwardhan built houses for Brahmins here in 1768) and is named after Hari Patwardhan. Haripur's riverside temples - the Sangameshwar Shiva temple at the sangam and the Bagetil Ganapati on the approach road - make it Sangli's main pilgrim-and-picnic suburb.

travel.road: 4 km from Sangli ST bus stand on the Haripur road; parking available for 2/4 wheelers.

visitor_information.best_time: June to October (best season per tourmet); evenings after 5 PM are peaceful. Shravan month is peak season.
